title: Spin-Boson Mappings in the Formalism of $f$-Deformations
authors: Vladimir A. Orlov, Liubov A. Markovich, Alexey V. Mikheenkov, Vladimir I. Man'ko
abstract: We develop a unified algebraic approach to spin-boson transformations based on the formalism of $f$-deformed oscillators. In the single-mode case, we show that the Holstein-Primakoff and Dyson-Maleev transformations, together with the interpolating $α$-family, arise as different factorizations of the same algebraically determined object. The standard spin-boson mappings can thus be interpreted as realizations of a common structure, which makes it possible to clearly separate the exact algebraic content on the physical subspace from effects associated with non-Hermiticity, the choice of metric, and extensions beyond the physical subspace. In the two-mode case, the same approach yields both deformed versions of the Jordan-Schwinger transformation and new exact two-mode realizations. Our results provide a unified description of known spin-boson transformations and naturally lead to new bosonic representations.
summary: This paper introduces a unified algebraic approach using f-deformed oscillators to map spin operators onto bosonic variables. It demonstrates that historically separate spin-boson transformations (like HP and DM) are mathematically related realizations of a single underlying algebraic structure. This provides a systematic tool for analyzing and potentially extending known models in quantum magnetism and quantum optics.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified algebraic framework to describe spin-boson transformations, aiming to reconcile various known mappings of the su(2) algebra.
main_result: It shows that standard mappings like Holstein-Primakoff, Dyson-Maleev, and Jordan-Schwinger arise as different factorizations of a single, underlying algebraic structure defined by f-deformed oscillators.
method: The authors use the formalism of f-deformed oscillators and employ finite-difference (Newton-series) expansions to derive exact algebraic relations on the finite physical subspace.
model_or_system: The model involves spin operators obeying the su(2) algebra, which are mapped onto bosonic variables. The analysis focuses on the single-mode and two-mode realizations of this algebra.
key_observables: The bosonic realizations of spin operators (S+, S-, Sz) and the algebraic constraints required for these operators to satisfy the su(2) commutation relations.
important_parameters: The spin quantum number (2S) and the deformation parameter (alpha).
main_assumptions: The derived algebraic identities are exact only on the finite physical subspace defined by the spin quantum number, not necessarily on the full infinite Fock space.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the general structure of spin-boson realizations of the su(2) algebra within the f-deformation formalism, showing the relationship between standard and generalized bosonic representations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general algebraic framework using f-deformed oscillators. It then analyzes the single-mode case, unifying HP, DM, and $\alpha$-family mappings. Subsequently, it addresses the two-mode case and concludes by deriving necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for the su(2) algebra to be satisfied by the bosonic operators.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, unified algebraic lens through which to view spin-boson models, which are central to understanding quantum magnetism, light-matter interactions, and quantum many-body physics.

The upper block corresponds to the standard matrix spin representation, from which the f-deformation approach generates a general class of bosonic realizations. This class contains both two-mode and single-mode representations. In the two-mode case, the diagram shows the standard N-conserving Jordan–Schwinger (JS) class, the squeezed Jordan–Schwinger transformation (sJS), and the possibility of more general realizations beyond the standard class.
